svg.title: Independent controls link neural activity to perturbation sensitivity

cc:Work.dc:title: Independent controls link neural activity to perturbation sensitivity
cc:Work.dc:description: Twelve panels show every EXP-005 control: core, lower transect endpoint, upper endpoint, and the retained near-edge comparison. Each column reports both step-size finite-time Lyapunov estimates and its certificate or finite-horizon classification. Rows plot all three neuron potentials, all three actual tanh activations, and state plus activation distances between baseline and perturbed trajectories. Axes use common scales across each row. The complete 300-unit records are shown, without smoothing or excluded controls. Irregular classification is limited to the measured horizons; raw perturbation distance includes possible phase displacement.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Independent controls link neural activity to perturbation sensitivity
All four controls retained; common initialization for each step-size run.
Header FTLE order: dt = 0.01 / 0.005; perturbation norm = 1e-6.
Common scales expose the distance contrast. Finite-horizon irregular support is not a chaos proof;
small same-time distances on a cycle can retain a neutral phase shift. No task-accuracy benefit is inferred.
